And Sinan laughed and said to him,
"Indeed, after you accept a rule,
that you shall not approach difficult diseases,
and you shall not cut a vein,
and you shall not give a purging root to drink."
And the old man swore:
"In nothing more than oxymel (sikangabin),
and what resembles it,
have I made use of."
And he permitted him to practice medicine.
Then on another day,
another physician came to him, a handsome youth.
And Sinan asked him,
"With whom did you study medicine?" And he replied,
"With my father."
And Sinan said,
"Who is your father?" And he replied,
"That old man who was with you yesterday."
And likewise Sinan the physician laughed and said to him,
"Go in peace, keeping the rule that you set for your father."
This Sinan, the Caliph Qahir coerced him,
and transferred him from paganism to the confession of the Arabs by force.
After Muqtadir, Qahir [reigned] one year and six months.
When Muqtadir was killed,
Munis advised the magnates to make Abu'l-Abbas, the son of the slain man, king.
For he said:
"When you do this, his mother will be comforted,
and his paternal aunt,
and his paternal aunt's sister,
and his foster-mother,
and without trouble they will bring out the gold that is in their possession."
The magnates, however, refused and said,
"No,
we have had enough of women.
With him who had only a mother,
all these things happened to us.
With him who alongside a mother would also have an aunt,
what then would happen to us?" And they all agreed,
and they brought Muhammad son of Muktafi and made him king,
and surnamed him Qahir.
When this man became king,
he greatly tormented the mother of Muqtadir.
And he hung her by a rope by one of her legs,
and he scourged her with his own hands on the deep and tender {OCR?} parts of her body,
so that she might reveal the gold.
And apart from what she confessed before the tortures,
nothing else was found in her possession.
And he also stripped the sons of Muqtadir and their mothers of gold.
It is said

when he was imprisoned in the palace,
